title: Daily Folic Acid Tablet Voice Alarm for Pregnant Women
title_te: గర్భిణీల కోసం రోజువారీ ఫోలిక్ యాసిడ్ మాత్ర గుర్తు
problem: Pregnant aunties in our neighborhood forget to take their daily iron tablets because they are busy cooking and fetching water all day.
idea: A daily Telugu voice reminder in Scratch and a printable tablet tracker. Here you can tick the days you remembered. Always take tablets exactly as the doctor or ANM said.

widgets.heading: ✅ This Week's Tablet Tracker
widgets.intro: Tick each day the tablet was taken, as the doctor or ANM advised.

bands.text: All 7 days! Great care for mother and baby.
Good! Try not to miss any day next week.
Many days missed. Set the voice alarm and ask the ANM for help.

questions.q: Who decides how many tablets to take?
questions.why: Always follow the doctor or ANM. Never change the amount yourself.

questions.q: A tablet was forgotten yesterday. What should she do?
options: Ask the ANM or doctor what to do
questions.why: Don't double up on your own. Ask the health worker.

questions.q: What helps her remember every day?
options: Same time daily with a voice alarm
Only when she feels like it
questions.why: Taking it at the same time daily, with a reminder, builds the habit.

questions.q: The tablet makes her feel sick. What should she do?
questions.why: The health worker can give advice. Don't stop without telling them.

how: Ask Gemini to write a short, kind Telugu reminder like 'Akka, it's time for your tablet. Take it as the doctor said.'
Record the message in Scratch using the Sound tab, or use the Text to Speech extension.
Make a big button sprite and a timer that plays the message at the time she chooses.
Open Canva and design a monthly tracker with tablet pictures and tick boxes.
Print the tracker and stick it near the kitchen.
Check the message with the ANM or ASHA worker before sharing.
prompt: I am a Class 8 student. Write 3 short, kind voice reminder messages in simple Telugu and English to remind pregnant women to take their daily tablet as advised by their doctor or ANM. Do not mention any dose.
